book.title: Yes! 50 Scientifically Proven Ways to Be Persuasive
book.author: Noah J. Goldstein, Steve J. Martin and Robert B. Cialdini

confidence_note: Chapter 34's title and thesis come from a library table of contents and a chapter summary that names New Coke as its example; the book text itself was not read, so how the book tells the New Coke case is unverified. New Coke facts are from Wikipedia. The old insulation '150 percent' figure and the Kahneman and Tversky link are not verified for this book and were dropped.
facts: Chapter 34 is titled 'What can you gain from loss?'; people respond more to what they may lose than to what they may gain.
A chapter summary gives New Coke as the example.
New Coke launched on 23 April 1985 and overwhelmingly beat regular Coke and Pepsi in taste tests, surveys and focus groups.
About 10 to 12 percent of testers said they felt angry and alienated at the idea of the change.
After launch Coca-Cola received over 40,000 calls and letters; the hotline took over 1,500 calls a day against about 400 before.
A group, Old Cola Drinkers of America, filed a class action that a judge quickly dismissed.
The original formula returned on 11 July 1985 as Coca-Cola Classic, 79 days after the launch.
scene_details: A hotline taking over 1,500 calls a day.
A blind taste test beaten by the new formula.
tension: A drink that won the taste tests lost the argument with the people who drank the old one.
opening_idea: Start with the taste-test win and the 79 days.

lessons.idea: Before changing something people rely on, count what they will feel they lose.
lessons.anchor: New Coke won taste tests yet drew calls and a lawsuit.

reflect_final: When you next change something other people rely on, what will they feel they are losing, even if you are sure they gain?

use_cases.situation: Moving a team to a new system
use_cases.move: New Coke won blind tests and still drew protest; I'll ask what people will miss in the old tool before I promote the new one.
Ask the household what they would hate to lose before you move anything.
Name what you will keep, then what changes.

pocket_idea: New Coke beat the old taste but lost to what people felt they were losing.

conversation_variants.punchline_idea: New Coke won every taste test and was gone in 79 days.
conversation_variants.thirty_sec_idea: The taste tests, the calls, the lawsuit, the 79 days.
